messages:
maya: Heads-up — need a quick design sync on a new "safeset" runtime config for scoped flags. Goal: let teams declare a scoped policy that includes per-scope rollout %, a quota cap, and an explicit audit/preview mode. Sketch below, want API shape + console UX + telemetry points. Thoughts?

tate: Quick q: is safeset per-tenant only, or can a single policy target multiple scopes (tenant + route + model-version)? Also: how strong do we need activation semantics (immediate vs staged)?

maya: Ideally allow multiple scope types in one policy. Activation should support "scheduled", "immediate" and "staged" (percent over time). Backend should support idempotent apply with optimistic lock. Example payload sketch: 

```json
{
  "policy_id": "safeset-2026-04-01",
  "scopes": [
    {"type": "tenant", "id": "acme-corp"},
    {"type": "route", "id": "embed-v2"}
  ],
  "rollout": {
    "percent": 20,
    "cohorts": [
      {"name": "beta-users", "match": "user.attr.beta == true"}
    ],
    "staged_schedule": [{"after_minutes": 0, "percent": 20}, {"after_minutes": 60, "percent": 50}]
  },
  "quota": {"tokens_per_minute": 2000, "burst": 5000},
  "fallback": {"model": "gpt-small", "route": "fallback-route"},
  "audit": {"emit": "breadcrumbs", "level": "detailed", "sample_rate": 0.1},
  "dry_run": true,
  "commit_token": "uuid-or-etag"
}
```

liam: +1 on commit_token (use ETag/If-Match style). For telemetry: emit three breadcrumb events: `policy.evaluated` (with evaluation_id), `policy.applied` (when route picks fallback), and `policy.decision` (true/false + cohort id). Include a short eval sample in console.

config-bot: Created RFC draft at https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1234 (auto-note) :robot_face:

tate: On API semantics: prefer PUT for full policy and PATCH for small edits, both require `commit_token` for optimistic concurrency. If commit_token mismatch -> 409 with `current_version` + `diff_preview` endpoint to help UI. Also: we should document merge semantics when multiple policies target same scope (priority, newest-wins vs explicit precedence).

maya: Console UX idea: "Simulate" toggle that runs X sample requests against the policy and shows acceptance rate, quota burn, and examples of fallback payloads. Show an inline diff preview of production traffic that would be affected. Add a prominent banner when `dry_run=true`.

liam: Quota interaction note: decide whether quota is enforced at routing layer (recommended) or post-hoc (metrics-only). Enforcing at router allows accurate throttling + early fallback, but needs fast replicated quota tokens or leaky-bucket sharding per region. If router-based, include `quota_shard_key` in policy so we can colocate counters.

tate: Implementation concerns: cache invalidation is tricky. Configs are cached heavily in edge routers and runtime. We need a versioned config blob and a small invalidation message (pub/sub) with `policy_id` + `version`. Avoid full cache flushes. Also consider `preview_id` so preview traffic doesn't affect live counters.

maya: Ops question: what telemetry fields are required for alerts? I propose: `policy_id`, `scope`, `version`, `evaluation_id`, `decision`, `quota_token_used`, `fallback_triggered` (bool), plus sampling fields. That should feed both dashboard and alert rules.

liam: Another edge: when combining multiple policies, we should compute a deterministic `effective_policy_id` and emit it so downstream traces can be correlated. Also record `policy_resolution_path` for debugging.

tate: Next steps: I'll stub API handlers (PUT/PATCH/GET preview/diff) and a replication hook. Liam can spike router quota sharding. Maya can mock the console preview UI. Let's sync tomorrow 9:30. Who owns RFC/PR?

maya: I'll take RFC -> PR, will add UI mock and sample telemetry schema. Assigning owners: maya (RFC + UI), tate (API + config replication), liam (router & telemetry). I'll drop a follow-up doc in #eng-platform with links. Thanks all :thumbsup:
